claim: To prevail on a sham litigation claim, plaintiffs must establish that the patent holder had no reasonable basis to believe its patent claims were valid or infringed, meaning a neutral observer would reasonably think the defendant was almost certain to be found not to have infringed if the suit went to judgment.
initial_reasoning: 967 F.3d 264 is the Federal Circuit case that articulated the “sham litigation” standard, holding that plaintiffs must show the patent holder had no reasonable basis to believe its claims were valid or infringed, and that a neutral observer would conclude the defendant was almost certain not to have infringed if the suit went to judgment. This directly supports the claim.
